content.text:
I reviewed the brief line by line against the 8-K release. Here is the check.

**Key issue:** the free cash flow figure. The release labels `~$8,700` million as **second‑quarter YTD 2026**, and footnote 6 marks it **estimated as of July 15, 2026**. The brief presents it twice as the quarter's free cash flow ("during the second quarter of 2026", "$6.2 billion in the same quarter last year"), converting a year‑to‑date estimate into a reported quarterly figure. Everything else in the Results, Segments and Outlook sections ties to the release, including the two dollar figures the brief omits (Innovative Medicine $16,384M, MedTech $8,926M) — omitted, but nothing stated wrongly.

One softer point worth flagging: the brief attaches the product driver commentary (DARZALEX, TREMFYA, STELARA's 760 bps) to Innovative Medicine's **7.8% reported** growth, whereas the release ties that commentary to **6.8% operational** growth. The 760 bps figure itself is quoted correctly.

facts.evidence: Reported second-quarter 2026 sales reached $25.3 billion, representing a 6.6% increase from the prior year period.
Second-quarter reported earnings per share (EPS) were $2.27, down 0.9% from the previous year.
Adjusted EPS for the quarter was $2.90, reflecting a 4.7% increase compared to the prior year period.
Innovative Medicine sales grew 7.8% reported, driven by strong performance in Oncology (DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, TECVAYLI, RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE), Immunology (TREMFYA), and Neuroscience (SPRAVATO, CAPLYTA).
The company increased its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance by $0.13 to a midpoint of $11.68, reflecting 8.2% growth at the midpoint.
Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year 2026 estimated reported sales guidance to a midpoint of $101.1 billion, representing 7.3% growth at the midpoint.
The company reported second-quarter free cash flow of approximately $8.7 billion, compared to $6.2 billion in the same quarter last year.
MedTech sales increased 4.5% reported, with operational growth of 3.6%.
Operational sales growth was 5.6%, while adjusted operational sales growth was 5.7%.

The release notes that STELARA had an approximate 760 basis points negative impact on Innovative Medicine growth. ... This growth was partially offset by declines in STELARA, REMICADE, IMBRUVICA, and ZYTIGA.

claims.claim: Reported second-quarter 2026 sales reached $25.3 billion.
Second-quarter 2026 reported sales represented a 6.6% increase from the prior year period.
Second-quarter 2026 operational sales growth was 5.6%.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted operational sales growth was 5.7%.
Second-quarter 2026 reported (GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.27.
Second-quarter 2026 reported EPS was down 0.9% from the previous year.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted EPS was $2.90.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted EPS rose 4.7% versus the prior year period.
Second-quarter 2026 net earnings totaled $5.5 billion.
Second-quarter 2026 net earnings decreased 0.1% year-over-year.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted net earnings were $7.1 billion.
Second-quarter 2026 adjusted net earnings were up 5.7% from the comparable period in 2025.
The company reported second-quarter free cash flow of approximately $8.7 billion, compared to $6.2 billion in the same quarter last year.
claims.note: The release presents ~$8,700M and $6,214M as second-quarter YTD (year-to-date) free cash flow, not the quarter alone, and footnote 6 states the 2026 figure is estimated as of July 15, 2026 rather than reported.

claims.claim: Innovative Medicine sales grew 7.8% on a reported basis in Q2 2026.
Innovative Medicine growth was driven by DARZALEX, CARVYKTI, TECVAYLI and RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE in Oncology, TREMFYA in Immunology, and SPRAVATO and CAPLYTA in Neuroscience.
Innovative Medicine growth was partially offset by declines in STELARA, REMICADE, IMBRUVICA and ZYTIGA.
MedTech sales increased 4.5% on a reported basis in Q2 2026.
MedTech operational sales growth was 3.6% in Q2 2026.
MedTech growth drivers included wound closure products, biosurgery products, electrophysiology products, Shockwave, contact lenses and trauma.
U.S. sales grew 7.3% on a reported basis in Q2 2026.
International sales grew 5.7% on a reported basis in Q2 2026.
International operational sales growth was 3.4% in Q2 2026.
Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year 2026 estimated reported sales guidance to a midpoint of $101.1 billion.
The full-year 2026 estimated reported sales guidance represents 7.3% growth at the midpoint.
The company increased full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance by $0.13 to a midpoint of $11.68.
The full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint reflects 8.2% growth.
Full-year 2026 adjusted operational EPS is estimated at a midpoint of $11.58, representing 7.3% growth.
The company generated approximately $8.7 billion in free cash flow during the second quarter of 2026.
claims.note: Repeats the period error: the ~$8,700M figure is second-quarter year-to-date and is an estimate as of July 15, 2026, not free cash flow generated during the quarter.

claims.claim: Johnson & Johnson announced an investment of more than $1 billion to strengthen U.S. vision manufacturing in Jacksonville, Florida.
The company entered into an agreement to acquire Firefly Bio, Inc. to expand its oncology pipeline.
The company entered into an agreement to acquire miniature radiofrequency tracking technology for its joint reconstruction portfolio.
The release notes STELARA had an approximate 760 basis points negative impact on Innovative Medicine growth.
Management states it cannot predict GAAP financial measures for 2026 due to uncertainties regarding legal proceedings and acquisition-related expenses.
The company cites a planned separation of its Orthopaedics business in its risk factors.
